spec_match.rationale: The consent story matches the sources: the spec's 'express permission' requirement, Chromium's transient-activation + confirmation-dialog behaviour (from the SubAppsAPIsAllowedWithoutGestureAndAuthorizationForOrigins policy definition), and the three prompt policies with exact enum values (1=AllowSubApps, 2=BlockSubApps, 3/unset=AskSubApps) and precedence (Blocked overrides Allowed overrides Default) taken verbatim from components/policy/resources/templates/policy_definitions/ContentSettings/*.yaml on Chromium main, fetched 2026-08-16.

interactive.rationale: Two real probes (window.subApps binding and navigator.userActivation reads, where the activating click itself demonstrates transient activation) plus a policy resolver whose select, origin input, allow/block textareas and scenario button all change the resolved outcome live.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises probing the real binding then resolving the three admin policies with documented precedence; the page delivers both stages in that order and labels which half is live versus documentation-driven.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the same-origin-on-both-lists conflict (blocked wins, via the one-click scenario), BlockSubApps default with no allow-list rescue, unset-behaves-as-Ask, and a non-isolated-app:// origin rejected with an explanation of why it can never reach these policies.

references.rationale: Links the chromestatus entry, all three enterprise policy pages, the spec's security & privacy section, and the sibling capability gate.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite records the un-automatable consent contract as an explicit manual assertion (add-user-consent-contract) that renders as blocked rather than a fake pass, exactly matching this page's honesty framing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome via the repo CDP harness (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this cloud environment): probe clicked with a real user gesture (CDP userGesture) → navigator.userActivation.isActive = true asserted alongside the honest 'subApps' in window = false; resolver asserted across five policy configurations (allow-list NO PROMPT, blocked-overrides-allowed ASK, default-2 BLOCKED, unset ASK, non-IWA origin rejected); zero console errors/warnings, zero network failures; post-interaction screenshot read (scratchpad/policy-after.png).

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts subapps-policy-probe with the real isActive reading, subapps-policy-resolved with the outcome class, and subapps-policy-invalid-origin for the rejection branch; the resolver output is never recorded as a platform result.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; fieldset/legend groups on bg-ivory with black borders; buttons pair background+color with 44px min height; form controls take width:100% with min-width:0 so the grid never overflows; the precedence chain reuses the flow-step pattern.

accessibility.rationale: Native fieldset/legend grouping with explicit for/id labels on select, input and both textareas; both outputs are aria-live and announced on the resolving activation; the precedence chain carries an aria-label while the arrows stay decorative; all controls keyboard-operable with focus-visible outlines.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Two mobile overflow defects found and fixed during this build (intrinsic form-control width, then unbreakable policy-name label tokens — 475px → 395px → 360px); final measurement at 360×740 DPR3 post-interaction: scrollWidth=360; desktop 1280 exercised with the full five-scenario script.

openQuestions.title: Verify prompt suppression on a managed ChromeOS 152 device
openQuestions.detail: The resolver encodes the documented policy semantics from the Chromium policy definitions, and the page is explicit that it cannot read a live managed-browser policy. On a managed ChromeOS 152 device with DefaultSubAppsWithoutPromptsSetting or the origin lists configured, confirm the real add() prompt behaviour matches the resolver's three outcomes, and note any divergence between the policy docs and shipped behaviour.

openQuestions.title: Track whether origin matching gains url-pattern semantics
openQuestions.detail: The two origin-list policies currently document exact isolated-app:// origins (example_value in the yaml), and the resolver matches exactly, saying so in its output. The older SubAppsAPIsAllowedWithoutGestureAndAuthorizationForOrigins policy accepts url patterns; if the prompt policies later adopt pattern matching, the resolver's matcher and its disclaimer need updating.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible form validation radio group select policy inputs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Group related policy controls with native fieldset/legend, give each control an explicit label, and validate on user action with feedback in a live region.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Two fieldsets (calling origin, policy values) with legends; select/input/textareas all label-bound via for/id; the resolve action announces outcomes and input errors through the aria-live output.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP interaction run 2026-08-16: five resolver scenarios asserted through the output element.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel form controls without horizontal overflow narrow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give form controls width:100% with min-width:0 inside grid tracks (intrinsic control width otherwise forces overflow) and allow long unbreakable tokens to wrap.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied after measurement caught two real defects: select/input/textarea gained box-sizing:border-box; width:100%; min-width:0 (fixed 475px viewport widening), and the 38-char policy-name label tokens were wrapped in code with overflow-wrap:anywhere on labels (fixed the remaining 395px widening).
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Bisected via CDP text-node scan; final mobile measurement scrollWidth=360 at 360px viewport.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status updates after button activation dynamic results
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Tie announcements to the user's activating interaction so assistive tech hears results exactly when sighted users see them.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both the probe and resolver write their aria-live outputs synchronously in the click handler; no state changes happen outside user activation.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP run: outputs asserted immediately after each dispatched click.

summary: New concept for the v152 milestone (no predecessor equivalent): pairs a genuinely live probe — the activating click demonstrates the transient activation a real add() consumes, via navigator.userActivation — with a resolver for the three ChromeOS 150+ enterprise prompt policies, using exact enum names, values and precedence from the Chromium policy definitions. Clearly labelled documentation-driven where a page cannot read live policy. Five policy scenarios plus the gesture probe exercised headlessly with zero console errors; two mobile overflow defects found and fixed during the build; mobile and desktop matrix pass.
